label: early original-phase input of g/l/a/n/q/b (steps 1-5)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99% of mass), at early positions t=1..5 (peak t=3; never t=0, essentially never on <DEL> or the copy phase). It is token-selective: inputs g, l, a, n, q, b carry about 84% of the mass, and first occurrences of a token are favored. Activation depends heavily on the preceding prefix: it is strongest when earlier tokens include d (especially first token d), q, or l (top examples look like d d q l ..., d s q g ...). This prefix dependence is not captured cleanly. Requiring seen([d,q,l]) only raises precision to about 0.25 and costs recall. The simple predicate covers most mass but has about 0.12 precision, because most early g/l/a/n/q/b inputs do not activate it.
